title: Measuring JF Dye Kinetics in the Brain of C57/Bl Mice
author: Boaz Mohar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5vmg646
materials: After 24h usually no more dynamics is obsureved.
Save the aligned stack and load in Matlab

steps.title: Anesthetize the Mouse
steps.instruction: Move the mouse to an induction chamber with 3% ISO and a flow of ~2L/min. Wait until the mouse takes ~1 breath per second.

steps.title: Prepare the Imaging Window
steps.instruction: Move the mouse to the microscope and clean the window using Q-tips and 70% ethanol.

steps.title: Configure Microscope Optics
steps.instruction: Select the objective and focus on the top of the cortex using room light or white light illumination.

substeps.instruction: Select either a 4x or 20x objective.
If using a 20x objective, add water above the window.
Lower the objective and focus on the top of the cortex.

steps.title: Set Up Illumination and Imaging
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate filter cube and illumination source for the dye and configure imaging conditions to ensure the baseline image takes ~10-20% of the dynamic range (above read noise level).

substeps.instruction: Set exposure to 50ms with 40 frames per timepoint (~2s total duration per timepoint), or 200ms with 10 frames if the signal is lower.

steps.title: Determine Illumination Settings
steps.instruction: Record baseline images at various illumination settings to prevent saturation after injection.

substeps.instruction: If using an LED, test 100mA, 500mA, 1A, and 2A driving currents with the same acquisition settings.
Use 500mA for the first image after injection, adjusting if too dark or saturated.

steps.title: Maintain Anesthesia
steps.instruction: If the animal is breathing faster than 1/s, remove it from the imaging rig and return it to the induction box.

steps.title: Capture Reference and Prepare Dye
steps.instruction: Record a white light reference image and prepare the dye aliquot.

substeps.instruction: Record a white light reference image to return to the same field of view without bleaching the signal.
Record the objective's location if possible.
Prepare a fresh dye aliquot.

steps.title: Perform Fluorescence Imaging
steps.instruction: Return the animal to the rig, navigate to the field of view using the white light reference, and begin imaging with the fluorescence light source.

substeps.instruction: Image at fast intervals (~1-3min) initially to capture rise and fast decay phases.
Increase intervals to 5-20min depending on dynamics.
After ~1h, increase intervals to more than 30min.
After ~4h, the animal can be removed from the rig and recordings performed at >2h intervals.

steps.title: Process Images
steps.instruction: Load images, calculate the mean for each timepoint, and save the mean images.

substeps.instruction: Load mean images into Fiji.
Use the stack sorter to move the first (baseline) image to the end of the stack.
Align the image stack using the Linear Stack Alignment with SIFT plugin.

steps.title: Analyze Kinetics
steps.instruction: Extract signal from the region of interest and fit a kinetic model.

substeps.instruction: Define a mask (ellipse or otherwise) of the imaged region of interest.
Median the pixels in the mask and subtract the baseline timepoint.
Fit a double exponential model to the remaining median pixels (excluding baseline) using the file creation date as the x-axis: y = a*e^(-1/(b*x)) + c*e^(-1/(d*x)).
Add a lower bound of 0 to all parameters.
If cells express a HaloTag, use the model: y = a*e^(-1/(b*x)) + c*e^(-1/(d*x)) + e.
Use the peak (usually the first point as the rise is very fast) as the first point for fitting.
